reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports the baseline's robust, pressure-invariant superconductivity, but the key mechanistic premises—that disorder averages fluctuations to stabilize coupling, and that composition tunes Tc via valence electron count and distortions—are not directly supported by E1 or E2. premises: Bcc HEAs with similar-sized atoms resist lattice distortions and pressure, preserving electronic structure
Compositional changes (e.g., Ti fraction) tune valence electron count and local distortions, shifting Tc
Configurational disorder averages out local fluctuations, stabilizing electron–phonon coupling
The baseline (TaNb)0.67(HfZrTi)0.33 has robust, pressure-invariant superconductivity with Tc ~7.5–8 K
The mechanism applies only to single-phase disordered bcc solid solutions
